title: White Sands near-Earth satellite search led by LaPaz and Tombaugh
place_text: White Sands Missile Range, New Mexico

tellings.quote: That same year, a very unusual project started at White Sands Missile Range.

plain: In 1953 a very unusual project began at White Sands Missile Range, a military test site in New Mexico: a search for small unknown objects circling close to Earth, led by the meteor scientist Lincoln LaPaz and the astronomer Clyde Tombaugh. Jesse Michels brings this up himself in a 2025 episode with the astronomer Beatriz Villarroel, and he points to the project's own final report, the Near Earth Satellite Project final report, as his source. He raises it because, if true, it would mean scientists were quietly hunting for unexplained objects near Earth years before any country had launched a satellite.
